extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities and interested parties (air carriers, pipeline companies, banks), their counsel, and other participants in Federal administrative dockets
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing applications, protests, petitions to intervene, reports, and for agency actions (suspensions, investigations, hearings) in Federal regulatory dockets (e.g., CAB, FPC, FDIC). Includes required forms, deadlines, and standards for reviewing rates and abandonment/ certificate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space-available requirement for parcel post service
rubrics_metrics.description: Shipments be accepted only on a space-available basis; parcel post rates justified where traffic utilizes available empty cargo space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s decision (Order E-20040) required that shipments be accepted only on a space-available basis to assure that parcel post traffic would utilize only such empty space and to differentiate the lower value of service under parcel post rates from regular service. The Flying Tiger Line proposal would eliminate the tariffs' current space-available requirement for westbound parcel post traffic receiving blocked-space service (except for contracted "blocked" amounts), effectively upgrading traffic to guaranteed space — a change the Board found suspect because low rates of the type established are justified on the ground that traffic uses available empty cargo space. The Board expressed serious reservations whether rates at the proposed levels would be economic except on a space-available basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for investigation or suspension of proposed rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rates and provisions may be investigated if they are, or will be, unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, unduly preferential, unduly prejudicial, or otherwise unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon consideration of complaints and other relevant matters, the Board/Commission may find proposed tariff revisions warrant investigation under statutory authority (e.g., Federal Aviation Act, Natural Gas Act) and institute proceedings to determine lawfulness and, if unlawful, to prescribe lawful rates and provisions. Example language: 'may be unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, or preferential, or unduly prejudicial, or otherwise unlawful.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proposed rates pending hearing and decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending hearing and decision, the rates and provisions described are suspended and their use deferred to a specified date; no changes allowed during the suspension period except by order or special permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board/Commission will suspend the proposed rates pending investigation and defer their use until a specified date (example: suspended to and including April 19, 1966), unless otherwise ordered, and prohibit changes in the suspended tariffs during the suspension period except by order or special permission of the Board/Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention and protest filing procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of intervention or petitions to intervene (or protests) must be filed in accordance with the agency's rules of practice and procedure (e.g., 18 CFR 1.8, 1.10, 1.37(f)) and applicable statutory/regulatory provisions by the published deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific docket notices set filing deadlines (examples: FPC allowed intervention filings on or before February 15, 1966; pipeline notices set January 27, 1966). Filings must be made with the agency docket office (e.g., Federal Power Commission, Civil Aeronautics Board) and in accordance with cited rules and regulations. Failure to file timely may affect ability to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of protests/petitions on hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If no protest or petition to intervene is filed within the required time, a hearing may be held without further notice and the applicant need not appear; if timely protest/petition is filed or the Commission determines a formal hearing is required, further notice of hearing will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure is used in certificate and abandonment applications: absence of protests triggers administrative review/hearing without further notice; timely protests convert matter to a contested proceeding with hearing scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Gas Act section 4(d) — 30-day notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(d) of the Natural Gas Act requires a 30-day notice period for rate filings; requests to waive this 30-day notice require good cause and may be denied if good cause is not shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bradley Producing Corp.'s request to permit an earlier effective date than the statutory 30-day requirement was denied for lack of good cause. Agencies will enforce the statutory notice unless adequate justification to waive is demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency policy on suspension length for producer increases related to purchaser increases
rubrics_metrics.description: General policy: suspend producer increases below the initial rate ceiling for only 1 day when contracts entered after General Policy No. 61-1; however, if the purchaser's rate increase (related to producers) is suspended for a longer period (e.g., 5 months), the producers' increases related thereto will also be suspended for the same period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission applies suspension lengths in light of related filings: because the purchaser's rate increase should be suspended for 5 months, producer increases directly related to that purchaser increase should likewise be suspended for 5 months, even though the usual policy for such producer increases would be a 1-day suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to make proposed rates effective despite suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that proposed increases be permitted to become effective without suspension or that suspension be limited (e.g., to 1 day) must show good cause; absent good cause, such requests will be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cleary Petroleum requested that its proposed rate increase be effective without suspension or limited to a 1-day suspension; the request was denied for lack of good cause. Agencies will deny requests seeking to circumvent suspension absent compelling justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDIC Call for Report of Condition — timing and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to section 7(a)(3) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act each insured bank is required to make a Report of Condition as of the close of business December 31, 1965, to the appropriate agency within 10 days after notice that such report shall be made; if the reporting date is a nonbusiness day, the preceding business day shall be the reporting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory statutory reporting obligation applicable to insured banks; agencies publish the call and specify the timing and handling of nonbusiness-day reporting dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and routing requirements for Reports of Condition by bank type
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bank type must use a specific form and route originals/copies to designated agencies: national banks — Comptroller Form (Call No. 456) to Comptroller, with signed attested copy to FDIC; insured State member banks — Federal Reserve Form 105 (Call 178) to the Federal Reserve Bank of the district, with signed attested copy to FDIC; insured State banks not members — FDIC Form 64 (Call No. 74) to FDIC; insured mutual savings banks not members — FDIC Form 64 (Savings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice specifies which form each class of bank shall use and to which agency the original and attested copies must be sent. Filers must follow these routing instructions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation instructions for Reports of Condition and Income/Dividends
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must be prepared in accordance with the agency-provided 'Instructions for the preparation of Reports of Condition' (and related instructions for Forms 64 and 73), dated in the years specified (e.g., January 1961; February 1961; December 1962; December 1961).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice identifies the specific instruction documents and dates that govern preparation; filers must follow the edition and any amendments noted. (References appear as: 'Instructions for the preparation of Reports of Condition by National Banking Associations,' dated January 1961; 'Instructions for the preparation of Reports of Condition by State Member Banks,' dated February 1961; 'Instructions ... on Form 64,' dated January 1961; and instructions for Forms 64 (Savings) and 73 dated December 1962 or December 1961 as applicable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for Annual Report of Income and Dividends on Form 73
rubrics_metrics.description: Insured mutual savings banks not members of the Federal Reserve System and certain insured State banks not members must make a Report of Income and Dividends for the calendar year on Form 73 (with revision/date specified) to the FDIC within 10 days after notice and prepared according to the cited instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual savings banks not members: Form 73 (Savings), revised December 1951, prepared per 'Instructions ...,' dated December 1962. Insured State banks not members (except DC and mutual savings banks): Form 73 (revised December 1961) prepared per instructions dated December 1961. Filers must use the correct revision of Form 73 and the matching instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining whether tariff revisions are economically justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies assess whether proposed rate reductions are economic (e.g., whether reductions would attract additional traffic, the resulting yields per ton-mile) and the potential impact on carriers' revenues; substantial reductions that would materially affect carriers may warrant investigation or suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating tariff filings, agencies consider claimed purposes (e.g., combining parcel post with other traffic to lower rates), submitted supporting data (or lack thereof), claimed public benefits, and potential adverse effects on competitors. Examples: proposed blocked-space reductions of 19–41% and resulting yields of 8.6–13.5 cents per ton-mile prompted the Board's concern that the reductions might be uneconomic and prejudicial to other carriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file and serve copies of orders and make parties to proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders instituting investigations or suspensions must be filed with the relevant tariffs and served upon named carriers/parties, who thereby become parties to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Copies of this order shall be filed with the tariffs and served upon Continental Air Lines, Inc., and The Flying Tiger Line, Inc., which are hereby made part ies to this proceeding.' Agencies use service and docketing to ensure parties' participation and to place the suspension on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of public convenience and necessity standard and application content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for certificates (e.g., pipeline construction and operation) must file applications describing the proposed facilities, estimated demand on design peak day, capacity deficiency, purpose of project, cost estimates, and financing; Commission will grant a certificate if a grant is required by the public convenience and necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices instruct that applications are on file and open to public inspection and set protest/intervention deadlines. If no timely protests and the Commission's review finds certificate is required by the public convenience and necessity, a hearing may be held without further notice; otherwise, hearings are scheduled if protests are filed or the Commission deems one necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment applications require section 7(b) permission and publish protest/ hearing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Permission and approval under section 7(b) of the Natural Gas Act are required to abandon facilities used for transportation of natural gas in interstate commerce; protests or petitions to intervene must be filed by the published deadline, and hearings will be held if protests are filed or the Commission determines a hearing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices for abandonment specify the facilities proposed for abandonment, background facts (e.g., facilities no longer needed due to depletion), and repeat the standard procedure that absence of protests will permit processing without appearance, whereas protests trigger contested hearings.
